flavor: Valdia lies beyond the edge of every chart.
Every living thing here carries an echo inside its body.
An echo, they say, is the sound of the first age, still refusing to fade.
Beneath the bedrock, the first power sleeps in layers.
The outpost pillars are beast bone. None has ever broken.
Tracks do not lie. Depth tells weight; spacing tells haste.
Grazed-down grass means the beast has only just fed.
In rain, beasts withdraw to the hollows. Hunt before it falls.
The Whitewater runs cold. The beast drinks there too.
A beast's shell cracks with light when the first power seeps to the surface.
Rage is the echo boiling over. The beast does not hate you.
A deeply wounded beast returns to its den. Only those who know the den go further.
The part that holds the most echo is the hardest. Break it, and it feeds the blade.
At the forge, the echo in a shard is woken with fire and moved into steel.
Lead shot cannot pierce an echoing shell. That is why hunters carry blades.
The first hunter to write 'the rock moved' never came back.
Skarv are cowards, but no one smells death sooner.
Watch which way the Grast herd runs. The beast is the other way.
A beast's name is the sound a hunter made after hearing its call.
The outpost keeps no map. Only the traces hunters carried home.
Deep in the gorge stands a ring of stones no human raised. No one goes near.
The bone walls buried in the strata are twice the size of any beast alive.
The old hunters say the continent is listening back.
In the silence after a roar, listen. You will hear the next step.
An echo never dies. It only thins. That, they say, is the nature of the first world.
A blade dulls as the echo drains from it. Whet it, and it returns.
Falling to your knees does not end the hunt. You only wake at the outpost.
When a beast sleeps, its echo stills. Its shell is never softer.
On mornings when the coastal fog lifts, a low sound reaches from the interior.
The first world still echoes.

killLines: The gorge is quiet, for now.
The blade answered. So did the beast.
Carry it home: the traces, the shards, and this silence.

timeLimit: The hour has passed. The beast remains in the gorge.
Back to the outpost before night. The beast will not run.
You could not close the distance today. The tracks will still be there tomorrow.
The hour exists to keep hunters alive. Withdraw.
The gorge has gone dark. Next time, start at dawn.
downs: Three times to your knees. That is enough for today.
The beast was strong. Knowing that is today's harvest.
Wounds heal at the outpost. The beast's habits stay in your head.
Remember where you fell. Next time, evade there.
Withdrawing is part of the hunt. Nothing is broken.
none: You left the hunt. The beast is still in the gorge.
Back to the outpost. The traces will not fade.
Not today. That, too, is a decision.
Whet the blade again. The gorge will wait.
You withdrew. When you return, the beast will be drinking in the same place.

areaCatch.base_camp: Whet the blade beneath the bone pillars

areaCatch.river: Beyond the water's noise, the beast
areaCatch.cave: Here the beast sleeps. Here it is softest

areaIntro.base_camp: A small outpost on the coast: pillars of beast bone and a stone forge. Hunters temper blades here, write down the traces, and set out for the gorge. The only place on the continent where a fire burns at night.
areaIntro.forest: Moss lies thick on the valley floor and swallows footsteps. Grast herds graze in the shade of fallen trunks, and beyond them there is always a larger print. When rain falls the moss glows faintly, showing how dense the echo runs.
areaIntro.river: A white rapid that splits the gorge. The beast drinks here and grinds the bank stones as it rolls. Keep away on flood days. Something lives under the water, the old hunters say.
areaIntro.cave: A hollow opening at the cliff's root. The first power runs dense inside, and the wounded beast withdraws here. Rock ledges hang loose from the ceiling. A sleeping beast's shell has gone quiet.

questDesc.vs01_hunt_valgaron: Valgaron, a primal beast in a shell of rock, holds the Mossfloor. By day it drives the grazing herds and drinks at the Whitewater; wounded, it withdraws to its den. Read the traces and face it.

itemDesc.valgaron_scale: A shard of rock-hard shell. Holds a faint echo.
itemDesc.valgaron_fang: A fang from jaws that crush their prey.
itemDesc.valgaron_claw: A great claw from the foreleg. Easier to take from a broken leg.
itemDesc.valgaron_horn: The horn. It can only be taken once broken.
itemDesc.valgaron_tail: An armour plate from a severed tail.
itemDesc.echo_core: An echo condensed inside a primal beast. It becomes the heart of a blade.
itemDesc.grast_hide: The thick hide of the grazing Grast.
itemDesc.grast_meat: Raw meat. Skarv are fond of it.
itemDesc.skarv_talon: The sharp talon of a carrion-eating Skarv.
itemDesc.vital_tonic: A decoction of echo-bearing herbs. You are defenceless while drinking.

valgaron.habitat: Verdant Gorge — the Mossfloor, the Whitewater, the Hollow
valgaron.ecology: Wears a shell like rock. By day it drives the Grast herds across the valley floor, drinks at the Whitewater, and sleeps in its den when tired. Deeply wounded, it withdraws to the den; when rain comes, it enters the hollow. Its rage is not hatred but the echo inside it boiling over. That is when the cracks in its shell begin to glow.
valgaron.hint: When the cracks glow, power gathers in the horn and it runs hot. The tail is thin at its root. The legs break from the front. While it sleeps, the echo in the shell goes quiet.
valgaron.sighting: The first hunter to write 'the rock moved' never came back. The second wrote down the depth of the tracks.
